## Open

## Resolved

### F-086 — `?inline` CSS is denied under Vitest but loads in the real app

> _2026-09-11 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

Loading `primereact/resources/themes/*/theme.css?inline` in vitest (jsdom) fails with
`Denied ID … pnpm/primereact@.../theme.css?inline`, because the Rush pnpm store lives outside the
vitest root and `server.fs.allow` rejects it. The real Vite app is unaffected: dev `fs.allow`
includes the workspace root and the build has no restriction, which a throwaway `vite build`
confirmed (the CSS string inlined to 178,538 chars).

Tests are unaffected because the Theme load effect catches the rejection — but do not assert on
`loadThemeCss` in vitest.

### F-087 — Model pages never populated their pivot-table dropdowns

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

On `meta/model` pages the pivot `dropdowns` prop was never populated, so the widget showed 'No
available options', and join-only pivots had no assignment mechanism at all. Fix: TableWidget
self-loads pivot dropdowns through `dropdownRegistry`/`portalDropdownList`, mirroring
DropdownWidget. Cost ~26 minutes and 14 attempts in req6.

### F-088 — A screenshot loop that cannot see pixels: verify via the live DOM

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

`view_image`/`screenshot_page` could not render pixels in this workspace, and a static `http.server`
hit port conflicts. The path that worked was to boot the dev server manually with
`PLAYWRIGHT_BACKEND_PORT=9083`, so the Vite proxy (default 8080) routes to the real backend — which
also fixes the 502s and the MLE-key errors — and then verify through the live DOM.

### F-089 — `ITabLayoutConfig.type` only accepts 'steps'

> _2026-08-21 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

Tabs are inferred by OMITTING `type`; passing `type: 'tabs'` fails lint with
`'tabs' not assignable to 'steps'`.

### F-151 — A `?inline` request fell through to the static handler and broke MIME

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

A Playwright failure on an `?inline` CSS import is a server-side problem, not a browser one. In Vite
8 such a request (`?inline`, `?url`, `?raw`) is only transformed when the resolved file passes the
dev fs access check (`checkLoadingAccess` on both the clean URL and the query-bearing URL); a file
reachable only through the module graph, such as a PrimeReact theme CSS under the pnpm store, falls
through to the raw static handler and is served with its real MIME type, which the browser rejects
for a module script.

Finding it meant unpacking the Playwright `trace.zip` and parsing `0-trace.network` for the exact
failing URL, because the test's HTML and diff output only show the visual consequence.

### F-152 — A menubar height change that looked like a global 1px shift

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

Half of the same Playwright failure was invisible in the screenshot diff, where it read as a global
1 px shift. Measuring the pixel rows and finally the live DOM identified the cause: `.p-menubar-end`
computed `display: block` because of stacked `menubarEnd` widgets.

### F-157 — `?direct` returns raw CSS where the default module request does not

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-browser · resolved_

When Playwright cannot write screenshot files into the workspace, one fallback is an isolated
`page.setContent()` harness — and getting the theme CSS into it needs Vite's `?direct` query, which
returns the CSS text verbatim. The plain `.css` request comes back as a JavaScript module and cannot
be injected into a `<style>` tag, so the obvious URL yields a harness with no styling.

Fetch the CSS with `?direct`, inject it, then magnify the harness to inspect 1-2 pixel bevel and
recess detail. Magnify with `transform: scale`, not `zoom` (which misbehaves on PrimeReact flex
panels), and clear any inline `zoom` before reading `getBoundingClientRect()`.
